notes: *flee* is added: `כָּסָה`'s lexeme is written by *hide*, so the supplied verb names an action the Hebrew never wrote, which rule 44's subtraction test and rule 20's supplied-lexical-verb clause both mark. The competing reading, taking *I flee ... to hide me* as one paraphrastic rendering of the verb, is named in that unit's note.

The *me* of *hide me* is retained with `כִסִּתִי` as the reflexive object the verb's own sense licenses (rule 44's `אִכַּף` → *bow myself* carve-out). The materially plausible alternative marks it added as a supplied object, since the Piel is not a reflexive stem and no object morpheme stands; the retained reading was preferred because *hide me* is how the ASV writes this verb used absolutely, and rule 2 does not split where the alternative is not clearly preferable.
The marginal *Hebrew Unto thee have I hidden* was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).
